purpose: Decision-consistency corpus for the Pudding-inspired pitch gate. Real-story entries are concise analytical annotations of public Pudding projects, not reproductions of article text. Anti-pattern entries are synthetic.
warning: Passing this corpus does not mean the system has learned The Pudding's taste. It only checks that the operational gate preserves intended continue/pivot/put-down distinctions.

pitch.argument: Off-grid timing can make a beat feel more human and distinctive even when conventional notation treats the deviations as errors.
pitch.why_you: I want to understand why tiny timing shifts change how groove feels in the body, not only how it looks in notation.
pitch.human_angle: The reader can connect an abstract timing measurement to the physical experience of hearing a beat move around the grid.
pitch.aha: The deviations are systematic enough to see and hear, yet subtle enough to vanish in ordinary averages.
pitch.distinctive_entry_point: The story treats sound itself as evidence and lets the reader compare timing rather than only reading an explanation.

data_plan.method: Align measured note timing with an explicit rhythmic grid and verify the compared excerpts.

visual_case.why_visual: The claim is perceptual: readers need synchronized sound and timing marks so they can see and hear the same microtiming difference.
visual_case.first_whiteboard: Sketch a beat grid whose marks move relative to a metronomic baseline.
visual_concepts: animated beat dots against a metronomic grid

interaction.rationale: Playback lets the reader perform the same perceptual comparison that the argument depends on.

pitch.prototype_plan: Build low-fidelity static timing frames and one synchronized audio prototype before production.
pitch.iteration_plan: Compare multiple timing encodings and keep the one whose change is easiest to hear and see on desktop and mobile.
kill_conditions: The timing differences cannot be measured reproducibly.
The audio/visual comparison does not change reader understanding beyond prose.

pitch.argument: National-anthem performances differ in measurable kinds of vocal embellishment, and those choices can be compared as a playful performance style rather than as a single duration ranking.
pitch.why_you: I am curious about the exact moments when a familiar ceremonial song turns into an individual performance.
pitch.human_angle: The human tension is between a fixed national ritual and a singer making the song unmistakably their own.
pitch.tone_or_obsession: loving but slightly ridiculous obsession with diva flourishes
pitch.aha: A custom score can separate different kinds of embellishment that a simple longest-anthem list would collapse.
pitch.distinctive_entry_point: Instead of ranking singers on one obvious metric, the entry point is a playful composite idea whose ingredients stay inspectable.

sources: performance audio and derived pitch traces
data_plan.method: Measure comparable vocal features by phrase, preserve the ingredients, and audit the composite score.
data_plan.fallback: Publish phrase-level comparisons without the composite score.

visual_case.why_visual: Pitch traces and synchronized audio make vocal choices legible at the exact phrases where they happen; prose alone cannot reproduce that listening comparison.
visual_case.first_whiteboard: Draw the same anthem phrase for several singers with pitch movement and embellishments aligned.
visual_concepts: guided audio clips followed by singer explorer

interaction.rationale: Audio controls let readers hear the specific pitch movement that the graphic highlights.

pitch.prototype_plan: Prototype one phrase with two singers before scaling the score and explorer.
pitch.iteration_plan: Test several encodings for pitch and ornament, then remove any scoring ingredient that readers cannot interpret.
kill_conditions: Comparable performances cannot be aligned reliably.
The custom score hides more than it explains.

pitch.argument: Apparent birthday-related mortality patterns can look spooky in raw counts, but careful baselines and uncertainty tests show which effects survive statistical scrutiny.
pitch.why_you: I want to test a folk claim that sounds plausible enough to repeat but strong enough to deserve skepticism.
pitch.human_angle: People attach meaning to birthdays and anniversaries even when population structure can create misleading patterns.
pitch.tone_or_obsession: skeptical curiosity about a statistical superstition
pitch.aha: An initially suggestive pattern weakens or changes once the correct comparison group and uncertainty are introduced.
pitch.distinctive_entry_point: The story begins with a claim many readers can intuit, then teaches why the denominator and null expectation matter.

data_plan.method: Construct observed and expected birthday-distance distributions and test uncertainty against explicit baselines.
data_plan.fallback: Use a narrower geography with complete dates and document representativeness.

visual_case.why_visual: The statistical argument is sequential; charts can reveal the raw pattern, expected baseline, and uncertainty in the same frame so the correction is perceptible.
visual_case.first_whiteboard: Start with a raw histogram, overlay the expected distribution, then reveal uncertainty.

interaction.rationale: Staged reveals prevent the baseline correction from being lost in a dense all-at-once chart.

pitch.prototype_plan: Storyboard raw, baseline, and uncertainty states before writing the final statistical explainer.
pitch.iteration_plan: Test whether each new layer changes the interpretation and remove any transition that only adds animation.
kill_conditions: Dates or denominators are too incomplete to form the baseline.
The apparent effect disappears before there is a meaningful teaching point.

pitch.argument: Common similes are far less fixed than memory suggests: a large corpus shows both formulaic defaults and imaginative alternatives around the same prompts.
pitch.why_you: I am curious why some comparisons feel inevitable in speech while others instantly reveal a speaker's voice.
pitch.human_angle: Readers can try to finish a phrase before seeing how thousands of other people actually completed it.
pitch.tone_or_obsession: language-pattern obsession with a game-like reveal
pitch.aha: Comparing your own completion with the long tail of corpus answers shows where cliché ends and invention begins.
pitch.distinctive_entry_point: The reader commits to an answer before the dataset reveals the distribution, making expectation part of the evidence.

data_plan.method: Normalize prompts and completions, preserve counts, and audit clustering before presenting the distribution.
data_plan.fallback: Use only prompts with enough observations to support stable comparisons.

visual_case.why_visual: The story depends on distributions of language completions and the contrast between a reader guess and corpus patterns; interactive reveal makes that difference felt.
visual_case.first_whiteboard: Ask for one completion, freeze the answer, then unfold the ranked corpus around it.

interaction.rationale: Committing an answer before the reveal turns the reader's expectation into a meaningful comparison, not decorative input.

pitch.prototype_plan: Test one prompt end to end, including input, reveal, and a no-JavaScript textual equivalent.
pitch.iteration_plan: Try multiple reveal timings and cluster layouts, then keep the version that makes the expectation gap clearest.
kill_conditions: The corpus is too biased to support the intended generalization.
Reader input does not materially change the reveal.

pitch.argument: A championship can be judged through an explicitly subjective ethical lens as long as the chosen criteria, weights, jokes, and limitations remain visible instead of masquerading as objective truth.
pitch.why_you: I want to interrogate sports celebration with a deliberately opinionated metric and see what happens when moral discomfort enters a familiar ranking ritual.
pitch.human_angle: Fans know the conflict: winning feels emotionally simple while the people and institutions behind it are not.
pitch.tone_or_obsession: provocative sports fandom with transparent subjectivity
pitch.aha: The interesting result is not one universal winner but how rankings swing when the ethical choices embedded in the score are inspected.
pitch.distinctive_entry_point: The story makes its normative assumptions part of the entertainment rather than hiding them behind pseudo-objective statistics.

sources: team records and documented ethical criteria
data_plan.method: Define every criterion, link supporting records, expose weights, and test sensitivity instead of presenting the score as objective fact.
data_plan.fallback: Publish the component evidence without an overall ranking if the composite becomes misleading.

visual_case.why_visual: A custom score needs visible components, annotations, and sensitivity to weights so readers can inspect how the judgment changes instead of accepting one magic number.
visual_case.first_whiteboard: Place component scorecards beside a rank that visibly moves as assumptions change.

interaction.rationale: Exploration exposes the subjectivity of the ranking by letting readers inspect components and sensitivity rather than hiding it.

pitch.prototype_plan: Prototype a few teams with all assumptions visible before scoring the full league.
pitch.iteration_plan: Stress-test the weights, remove criteria that cannot be defended, and compare a non-ranked alternative before production.
kill_conditions: The evidence behind key criteria cannot be sourced consistently.
The composite score implies a false objectivity that annotations cannot repair.

pitch.argument: Relationships that look similar in a snapshot can follow very different emotional trajectories, and repeated survey responses reveal those paths better than a single satisfaction score.
pitch.why_you: I want to see relationships as changing stories rather than reducing them to one average about happiness or longevity.
pitch.human_angle: Readers recognize uncertainty, repair, drift, and stability in individual trajectories rather than abstract demographic rows.
pitch.tone_or_obsession: curiosity about narrative hidden inside longitudinal data
pitch.aha: The same endpoint can be reached through very different sequences, so averages can erase the shape of a relationship.
pitch.distinctive_entry_point: Longitudinal responses are treated as stories with turning points rather than as rows in a summary table.

data_plan.method: Preserve respondent trajectories, define comparable measures, and protect privacy while auditing attrition and missing waves.
data_plan.fallback: Use aggregate archetypes when individual trajectories cannot be shown safely.

visual_case.why_visual: The evidence is temporal and individual: trajectories and annotated transitions let readers perceive patterns that a prose summary or aggregate table would flatten.
visual_case.first_whiteboard: Draw several relationships as parallel timelines that diverge, recover, or remain stable.
visual_concepts: guided archetypes followed by trajectory explorer

interaction.rationale: After guided archetypes, exploration lets readers compare paths without reducing every relationship to one rank.

pitch.prototype_plan: Prototype a small anonymized set of paths before deciding how much individuality can be safely retained.
pitch.iteration_plan: Compare individual paths, archetypes, and aggregate summaries and keep only the level that remains legible and ethically defensible.
kill_conditions: Privacy constraints prevent a responsible representation of individual change.

pitch.question: What is happening in the global EV industry?
pitch.why_you: I want a comprehensive overview of this large market for a general audience.

data_plan.method: Combine country production, sales, and market-share tables into a normalized dataset.

visual_case.why_visual: There are many numbers and charts.

pitch.argument: A proprietary dataset would reveal which private clinics have the largest untreated mental-health demand, making access gaps visible at neighborhood scale.
pitch.why_you: I care about the mismatch between need and care because national averages hide the dead ends patients encounter locally.
pitch.human_angle: Patients experience access as a local wait, distance, or closed door rather than as one national statistic.
pitch.aha: The intended reveal is a neighborhood mismatch between demand and capacity that national aggregates cannot expose.
pitch.distinctive_entry_point: The entry point follows a patient's local search for care rather than beginning with a national prevalence ranking.

visual_case.why_visual: A local map would make demand and clinic capacity mismatch visible block by block and expose distance as part of the access problem.
visual_case.first_whiteboard: Overlay demand, clinic capacity, and travel-time catchments.

interaction.rationale: Exploration would let readers inspect the local mismatch at neighborhood scale.

pitch.prototype_plan: Prototype with a tiny authorized sample before any public implementation.
pitch.iteration_plan: Compare map and non-map forms once a lawful dataset exists.
kill_conditions: No lawful public fallback can answer the same question.

pitch.argument: A newly published tax rule creates a hidden paperwork burden for freelancers because its definition conflicts with the language used by the most common filing guidance.
pitch.why_you: I keep seeing freelancers misunderstand the same sentence and want to explain the contradiction precisely.
pitch.human_angle: The human angle is the anxiety of ordinary people reading two official texts that seem to tell them different things.
pitch.aha: The central reveal is a legal-definition mismatch visible only after comparing the wording and exceptions carefully.
pitch.distinctive_entry_point: The entry point is one contradictory sentence experienced repeatedly by people filing taxes.

data_plan.method: Trace definitions and exceptions to the controlling texts and verify examples against the rule.
data_plan.fallback: Narrow the piece to the exact conflict if broader impact counts are unavailable.

pitch.prototype_plan: Test whether a text-only explainer is clearer than any visual treatment.
pitch.iteration_plan: Compare a prose memo with one annotated-document prototype before choosing format.
kill_conditions: The texts do not actually conflict after legal review.
The claimed burden cannot be supported beyond anecdote.

pitch.argument: City recycling rates have diverged since 2018, with policy timing explaining part of the difference between otherwise comparable municipalities.
pitch.why_you: I want to understand why some cities improved while similar neighbors stalled after adopting different collection rules.
pitch.aha: The divergence begins near specific policy changes rather than moving smoothly with income.
pitch.distinctive_entry_point: Pair cities that look similar before the policy change and follow them as rules diverge.

data_plan.method: Normalize recycling tonnage and households, align policy dates, and validate comparable denominators.
data_plan.fallback: Use only city pairs with stable definitions.

visual_case.why_visual: A paired time series can make divergence and policy timing visible in the same frame.
visual_case.first_whiteboard: Two paired lines with policy annotations.

interaction.rationale: A 3D wheel makes the page feel more interactive.

pitch.argument: Housing affordability has worsened fastest where rent growth outran local wages after 2020.
pitch.aha: Some cities with moderate rent levels still deteriorated fastest because wages lagged.

data_plan.method: Join annual rent and wage series on consistent geographies and recompute change from the raw data.

visual_case.why_visual: The divergence can be seen in a slopegraph or paired time series.

pitch.prototype_plan: Build one static slopegraph before implementation.
